issues.description: SR4's arithmetic-consistency logic is only triggered when the remediation text explicitly mentions a 'second decrement' or 'no-cancel' phrase. There is no shipped mutant/test case demonstrating a submission that trips this specific SR4 branch (double-decrement inconsistency) while passing SR1-SR3; the validation report confirms 'uncovered_requirement' for SR4 with 0/1 targeting mutants detected. This means the security-relevant behavior for SR4 (rejecting arithmetically-inconsistent remediations) is present in code but unverified/untriggered by the test suite.
issues.evidence: per_requirement_coverage.SR4: {covered: false, mutants_detected: 0, mutants_targeting: 1}; issues: [{issue: uncovered_requirement, detail: 'SR4 has no targeting mutant detected by its own check'}]

issues.description: The naive baseline correctly fails all SR checks and most FR checks, but FR4 passes for the baseline (confidence/method fields are trivially valid), which is expected/acceptable since FR4 is a narrow type check unrelated to correctness of the finding.

recommendations: Add a targeted mutant/scratch submission to the test harness that describes 'decrement on entry to COMPARE' plus an explicit second decrement in CHECK_DONE on failure (with no offsetting restore) to concretely exercise and validate the SR4 double-decrement rejection branch, since current mutation testing shows this branch is never hit (0/1 targeting mutants detected).

Consider adding an additional mutation case that passes SR1-SR3 but describes an arithmetically-inconsistent remediation, to raise the mutation_score above the current 0.875 and confirm SR4 is a live, discriminating check rather than dead code.

Optionally strengthen the corroborative iverilog simulation (tb_stateskip.v) to also verify a hardened reference implementation against the fault-free lockout sequence, since currently it only demonstrates the vulnerability, not remediation correctness, even though this is explicitly optional per the spec.
